topic: Uniform Circular Motion and Centripetal Force
key_concepts: An object accelerates when its speed changes, its direction changes, or both
Uniform circular motion is motion at constant speed along a circular path
The period T is the time required for one complete revolution around the circle
Speed in uniform circular motion is calculated as v = 2πr/T
The velocity vector in circular motion is tangent to the circular path
An object in uniform circular motion experiences centripetal acceleration
Centripetal acceleration magnitude is ac = v²/r
Centripetal acceleration always points toward the center of the circle
A net inward force called centripetal force is required for circular motion
Centripetal force magnitude is Fc = mv²/r
Centripetal force direction always points toward the center of the circle
Tension in a string can supply the centripetal force that keeps an object moving in a circ
